source: MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture, banana cultivation techniques manual, 2019, section VI.3 (harvest method)
text: Harvesting is normally done by a two-person team: before cutting, prepare the harvesting knife and a soft support (cloth or bag) to catch the bunch, so it is not dropped or bruised. One person supports the weight of the bunch from underneath while the second person cuts the pseudostem partway and gently lowers the whole stem so the bunch comes down under control rather than falling. The bunch is typically wrapped or cushioned during this process to prevent the fruit from being bruised or scraped against the stem, the ground, or other bunches. After cutting, individual hands (clusters of fingers) are separated cleanly from the main stalk with a knife, ready for sale or further processing by hand/cluster rather than as a whole bunch.
